meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Gibraltar (British Overseas Territory) with the corporate vehicle incorporated in the Cayman Islands (British Overseas Territory) and registered as an overseas company in Gibraltar under Part 12 of the Companies Act 2014
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law legal system; both Gibraltar and the Cayman Islands apply English common law as binding precedent, subject to Privy Council appeal supervision, with an offshore-special-territory regulatory overlay and locally enacted statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2019, in force 1 January 2021)
Gibraltar-Isle of Man Double Taxation Agreement (2010)
UK-Cayman Islands Tax Information Exchange Agreement (in force 2010)
US-Cayman Islands Tax Information Exchange Agreement (in force 2001, as amended)

OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS - Pillar Two GloBE Model Rules (Gibraltar domestic implementation effective for accounting periods beginning on or after 31 December 2024; Cayman Islands committed to implementing the GloBE rules for multinational groups within scope)
Hague Apostille Convention 1961 (extended to both Gibraltar and the Cayman Islands by UK declaration)
UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement (relevant for EU-market customs and digital-trade access; the EU-Gibraltar framework treaty is under negotiation and not yet ratified)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Gibraltar: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (as amended by the Proceeds of Crime (Amendment) Regulations 2022); Sanctions Act 2019; Companies Act 2014 sections 263-285 (beneficial-ownership records and overseas-company registration); GFSC AML/CFT Handbook (2023 Edition); Money Laundering Regulations 2020. Cayman Islands: Companies Act (2023 Revision); Proceeds of Crime Act (2021 Revision); Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2023 Revision); Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Law (2023 Revision); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2023; CIMA AML Guidance Notes (2023). UK-extension overlay: Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018 (extended to Gibraltar and the Cayman Islands by Order in Council).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the Cayman Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2023 establishes a restricted-access central register available only to the Registrar, CIMA, the Cayman Financial Reporting Authority and competent law-enforcement authorities upon legal process; no public access. Nominee arrangements are lawful but the underlying beneficial owner must be disclosed to the licensed corporate service provider. In Gibraltar, the overseas-company branch files director and authorized-representative details with the Companies Registry, while UBO particulars are held privately by the Gibraltar corporate service provider and disclosable to the GFSC, the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit and tax authorities on request).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Cayman Exempted Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Cayman Islands competent authority / UK FCDO legalisation office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Registrar-stamped copy)
Certificate of Good Standing and current registry extracts
Certificate of Incumbency (current directors, secretary, registered office and registered agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Cayman corporate service provider (registered office holder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Cayman notary public + Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Register Extract and UBO Declaration (each UBO with passport/proof-of-address)
Board Resolutions approving Gibraltar branch/overseas-company registration, appointment of the Gibraltar resident agent for service of process, and delegation of bank signatory authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Cayman Exempted Company

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies, proof of residential address and PEP self-declaration of all directors, shareholders and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the home jurisdiction of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Apostille member states; Consular Legalization through the relevant consulate or British Embassy for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and six-month source-of-wealth documentation for founding shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the issuing jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories and the Gibraltar branch manager against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List; UK OFSI consolidated and asset-freeze lists (extended to Gibraltar and the Cayman Islands by Order in Council); EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (required for EU payment rails); OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (required for USD clearing and Stripe or platform credit-card processing); Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit advisories; CIMA enforcement and disqualification notices; UK Money Laundering Regulations designated-risk indicators. Screening must be repeated on an event-driven basis and in any event at least annually. PEP status is determined under the GFSC AML/CFT Handbook and CIMA Guidance Notes; senior foreign PEPs, UK PEPs and domestic PEPs trigger enhanced due diligence comprising documented source of wealth, senior-management approval of the relationship, and enhanced ongoing transaction monitoring. Notwithstanding the Low_Risk_Standard banking classification of the dental-aligner e-commerce model, simplified due diligence is not available as a substitute for mandatory identity and UBO verification; enhanced measures apply on any PEP or sanctions-list hit.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.commercial_strategic_role_en: Pan-European digital-trade gateway, rapid low-cost online incorporation, and innovative EMI (electronic money institution) bank-account onboarding corridor between the Cayman Islands and Gibraltar.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Primary: Cayman Islands General Registry, Companies Registration e-Services (https://www.ciregistry.ky) for the exempted-company name reservation and incorporation. Secondary: Gibraltar Companies Registry (Companies House Gibraltar) operated within the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (https://www.companieshouse.gi / https://www.fsc.gi) for the overseas-company (branch) registration under Part 12 of the Companies Act 2014.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the sole official corporate language in both the Cayman Islands and Gibraltar. The company name must be expressed in Latin-script characters; no transliteration into a local script is required by either registry. The name must end with or incorporate the word Limited or the abbreviation Ltd. For the Gibraltar branch, the exact Latin-script rendering of the Cayman name must be registered unless the Gibraltar Registrar approves an alternative trading name under section 265(5) of the Companies Act 2014. Numerals, punctuation and standard corporate suffixes are acceptable if not misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Cayman: tokens suggesting Crown or government patronage - Royal, Imperial, Government, Commonwealth, Crown, Authority, Municipal - require a government non-objection letter or are refused outright under section 31 of the Companies Act (2023 Revision)
Cayman: CIMA-consent tokens - Bank, Banking, Trust, Trustee, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Securities, Mutual Fund, Fund, Broker, Fiduciary
Gibraltar: GFSC-consent tokens - Bank, Banking, Fiduciary, Insurance, Assurance, Fund, Securities, Financial, Clearing, Deposit, E-Money

Gibraltar professional-regulation flags - Dental, Orthodontic, Medical, Clinical, Surgical, Orthodontic, Pharmaceutical - trigger referenced scrutiny under the Gibraltar Medicines Act, the Medical Devices Regulations 2013 and the EU MDR 2017/745 framework, requiring proof of a valid UK MHRA or EU Notified Body registration and a clear statement that the entity manufactures devices and does not practise dentistry

Cayman and Gibraltar: professional-body or institutional terms - Solicitor, Advocate, Lawyer, Auditor, Accountant, Chartered, Bar, Chamber of Commerce, University, College, Institute, Foundation, Association, Council, Charity - require evidence of the corresponding professional authorization or official registration

Names identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name on the Cayman register (Companies Act section 30) or the Gibraltar register (Companies Act 2014 section 42) are refused; confusingly similar names may also be challenged under the Gibraltar Trade Marks Act 2000
Any name constituting a criminal offence or that is offensive, deceptive or contrary to the public interest under Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 section 42(2) or Cayman Companies Act section 31

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss. 14-20 (incorporation and registration), ss. 21-25 (registered office), ss. 94-98 (first directors and secretary), together with the Companies (Fees) Regulations 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar (online via companieshouse.gi)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 2014; one Ordinary Share of GBP 0.01 at par, or a share of no par value, suffices. No escrow account or capital certification is mandated for a non-financial trading company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the issue and allotment of 1,000 Ordinary Shares of GBP 0.01 each to the subscribers at par is hereby approved; (2) the registered office of the Company shall be situated at 5/2 Cornwall's Lane, Gibraltar, GX11 1AA; (3) [Director A], [Director B] and [Director C] be and are hereby appointed as first Directors of the Company, and [Secretary] be appointed as Company Secretary; (4) the Directors be and are hereby authorized to file the Memorandum and Articles of Association, open corporate bank accounts, and register with the Income Tax Office; (5) any Director may execute all documents necessary to comply with the Companies Act 2014.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (online search portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the Companies House electronic portal and submit a name reservation application. The proposed name must not contain restricted words (e.g., 'Bank', 'Insurance') without prior consent, and must not conflict with existing registered trademarks. Name reservations are valid for 28 days.
required_dossiers: Consent to act forms for directors (draft)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused under section 16 of the Companies Act 2014, file a re-consideration request with the Registrar within 14 days or submit an alternative name reservation immediately via the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Gibraltar or a jurisdiction with apostille) and legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in conformity with the Companies Act 2014 model articles or bespoke articles. Each subscriber must initial every page and sign the final execution page before a certified notary or independent witness. Notarized documents shall be delivered to the Gibraltar filing agent.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity and residential address for each subscriber
Consent forms for first directors and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies House queries the M&A, submit a revised instrument conforming to the model articles; re-execution before a notary is sufficient to cure defective signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the executed M&A, registered office consent, and director/secretary consents via the Companies House online portal or physically at the Registry. Pay the applicable filing fee. The application may be expedited for same-day processing.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (two copies)
Proof of payment of official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond in writing to the Registrar within 21 days with corrected Form 1; any defective statutory declarations must be re-sworn and re-submitted with a late-filing explanatory letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Tax Residency Determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies; Income Tax Office, Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful compliance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with a company registration number. The company then registers with the Income Tax Office for a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN) and files a Tax Residency Status Form to confirm well-managed-and-controlled status outside Gibraltar for non-residence treatment.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (final stamped copy)
Tax Residency Status Form (available from Income Tax Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is withheld, rectify all deficiencies noted on the query slip and re-file within 14 days; if the Registrar acts ultra vires beyond 30 days without cause, seek judicial review through the Supreme Court of Gibraltar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar-licensed bank or reputable EMI; Income Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account with the Certificate of Incorporation and M&A, executing authorized signatory mandates. Apply for the Gibraltar TIN from the Income Tax Office, and register for employers' social insurance contributions if hiring locally. The bank must complete AML/KYC checks.
required_dossiers: Directors' identification and proof of address
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TIN application is delayed, request an expedited review from the Commissioner of Income Tax; for bank rejection, present audited or notarized source of funds documentation or re-apply at an EMI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 14 days of incorporation, file the register of beneficial owners with the Companies House Beneficial Ownership Registry. Maintain statutory books, issue share certificates, and file the annual return and exemption declaration (if applicable) with the Registry under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2019.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a non-compliance notification, file the Beneficial Ownership Register within the curative 30-day period and pay the standard late fee; failure to cure may result in a penalty, which can be mitigated by voluntary disclosure and full compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry for Business and Enterprise, HM Government of Gibraltar, in coordination with the Gibraltar Health Authority for medical device conformity
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating Permit for Medical Device Manufacturing (Class IIa)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability, Heritage and Climate Change (DESHCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Environmental Screening for Light Manufacturing; Full EIA Report not anticipated for thermoforming and trimming operations)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Trade effluent must meet the Sewerage (Trade Effluent) Regulations limits (pH 6.0-9.0; BOD ≤ 400 mg/L; TSS ≤ 350 mg/L); process air VOCs must not exceed 50 mg/Nm³; plastic scrap must be segregated and disposed of via a licensed waste carrier under the Waste Regulations 2011 (Gibraltar).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service under the Fire Precautions (Workplace) Regulations; Structural Load Clearance for thermoforming and storage areas issued by a chartered engineer approved by the Building Control Authority; and Occupational Health and Hygiene Clearance from the Health and Safety Executive (Gibraltar) covering machine guarding, noise ≤ 85 dB(A) action limit, and PPE protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar, 198 Main Street, Gibraltar; online portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/; Companies House Gibraltar: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/en/companies-house
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign legal entity (e.g., a Cayman Exempted Company) must first be registered as an 'overseas company' with the Gibraltar Companies House if it establishes a place of business in Gibraltar. It must file certified constitutional documents, details of directors, and a registered office address in Gibraltar. Upon registration, the company is issued a Gibraltar company number, which also serves as the corporate TIN for Income Tax after the company completes the Income Tax registration form (available from the Income Tax Office) and provides evidence of overseas tax residency. The Commissioner will issue a Gibraltar Assessment (TIN) within 10 business days. If the company has a permanent establishment subject to tax, it must also file annual returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (non-resident foreign company; no Gibraltar income tax absent permanent establishment)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cayman Islands: Exempted Company may elect for a 20-year tax exemption undertaking under the Cayman Tax Exemption Law. Gibraltar: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist; Gibraltar imposes corporation tax on territorial basis at 12.5%; foreign entities are not subject to tax on offshore/foreign-source income unless such income derives from a permanent establishment in Gibraltar. There are no 'pass-through' or 'transparent' elections available for a limited company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST – Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area; indirect taxation consists of customs/import duties, excise duties, and stamp duty. No general sales/use tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable; no indirect tax registration obligation in Gibraltar for sales/use or VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or e-invoicing mandate; no digital stamping. Imports into Gibraltar are processed through the Gibraltar Customs Department's electronic GDPS system; exports to the EU/UK require customs declarations through licensed brokers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: As no Gibraltar VAT exists, the concept of statutory zero-rating cannot apply. Dental clear aligner sheets physically exported from Gibraltar to third countries are treated as outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect taxes and thus no Gibraltar output tax is charged. To avoid import duty leakage upon final re-export, the company must comply with inward processing/end-use relief requirements of the Gibraltar Customs Department. Where goods are sold from Gibraltar to UK/EU customers, the supply is treated as occurring outside Gibraltar for indirect tax purposes; import VAT may be charged by the destination State.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Gibraltar Income Tax Office may investigate any claim for tax exemption or non-taxation. If a company falsely represents goods as exported to obtain an export certificate or to avoid tax, the Commissioner may raise an assessment on the full sale value, apply interest at statutory rates, and impose penalties up to 150% of the tax due. For customs/duty fraud, the Customs Department may seize goods and impose civil penalties up to GIP 10,000 per declaration; criminal conviction can result in imprisonment up to two years. In addition, the Cayman Islands tax exemption certificate may be revoked if the entity engages in illicit activities in contravention of the Tax Exemption Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the integrated financial regulator and de facto monetary supervisor of Gibraltar. Currency issuance and monetary stability are governed by the Currency Notes Act (Cap. 96) under the HM Government of Gibraltar, with the Gibraltar pound (GIP) pegged at 1:1 to the Bank of England sterling. The Bank of England indirectly anchors monetary policy; no separate Gibraltar central bank performs open-market operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility with zero exchange-control restrictions under the Exchange Control Act framework (now substantively liberalised). GIP and GBP circulate interchangeably at par within the territory; conversions to EUR, USD, and other major currencies are unrestricted. Profit remittances from a licensed trading subsidiary to a Cayman parent attract no Gibraltar withholding tax, dividend tax, or capital gains levy, and no prior central-bank authorisation is required for outward remittances. Post-Brexit, Gibraltar retains its own currency regime outside the European System of Central Banks but benefits from UK sterling stability and free capital flows within the UK's residual territory network.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or repatriation timeline applies in Gibraltar. There is zero mandatory conversion ratio; dental aligner export receipts denominated in USD, EUR, or GBP may be retained indefinitely in original currency. This reflects Gibraltar's Euro-Mediterranean trade neutral status and the absence of a distinct exchange-control statute mandating conversion. The only administrative requirement is accurate recording of trade income for GFSC-licensed activity and Companies House (Gibraltar) financial disclosure purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency GBP/EUR/USD) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (private banking and corporate deposits)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM (conditionally viable). UK-FCA-authorised Electronic Money Institutions such as Wise Business, Airwallex, and Revolut Business can onboard the Gibraltar operating company as a corporate client, but post-Brexit they typically classify Gibraltar as a third-country EEA-adjacent territory, triggering enhanced KYC reviews, potential restrictions on EUR SEPA direct-debit rails, and a 30-90-day onboarding timeline. Offshore digital EMIs domiciled outside the EEA or UK (e.g., Bermuda or BVI-licensed facilitators) are NOT recommended as primary settlement banks because Gibraltar-licensed correspondent clearing is required to participate in UK Faster Payments and CHAPS. An EMI account may serve as a disbursement sub-ledger for Stripe payouts, provided the master treasury account remains at a Tier-1 Gibraltar commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar banks currently mandate physical attendance of at least one natural person executive director or the beneficial owner for an in-person identification interview at the bank's corporate centre in Gibraltar or via a notarised video interview witnessed by the bank's international introducer desk. Remote opening is permitted on a case-by-case basis only where (i) the beneficial owner is a PEP-free professional investor with a Gibraltar-licensed registered agent as introducer, and (ii) a sworn affidavit identifying the structure is apostilled in Cayman and the UK. For a Cayman Exempted Company holding a Gibraltar branch, standard practice is a physical sign-off at either the Gibraltar or London representative office of the bank within 90 days of account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman Exempted Company opacity and offshore tax-exempt status flagged under Gibraltar's AML/CFT Regulations 2022 as a higher-risk cross-border legal vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing from the Cayman Islands General Registry; current Memorandum and Articles of Association; Register of Directors and Register of Members (notarised); land, tax, and economic-substance declaration confirming Gibraltar branch trading substance; sourced funds evidence (6 months of shareholder bank statements and board-minuted capital contribution resolution)

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential unlicensed financial activity concern due to Stripe platform payment collection and settlement volumes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant services agreement with Stripe Payments Europe Ltd (Irish entity), demonstrating the Gibraltar entity's business as a licensed medical-device supplier, not an e-money issuer; revenue model narrative; product registration under Gibraltar Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency or UK MHRA for dental aligners; capex forecast

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing physical trading substance in Gibraltar, indicating possible brass-plate operation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar rental or serviced-office agreement, local payroll mandate for supervisory staff, Gibraltar Economic Substance Act annual return with banking/finance licence waiver certification, and purchase orders from EU dental laboratories evidencing genuine supply-chain activity

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Conflicting VAT/tax status of Cayman shareholder vis-à-vis Gibraltar permanent establishment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar tax residency certificate, HMRC territoriality memorandum, legal opinion on no Gibraltar corporate tax liability under Income Tax Act for exempt-zone parent, and consolidated treasury policy letter of comfort from the CFO

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from the Cayman parent must route via SWIFT MT103 with payment field 70 (Remittance Information) stating purpose code 'EQUI' (Direct Investment – Equity Capital) or, where funding is structured as shareholder loan, code 'LOAN'. The wire must originate from the Cayman entity's own bank account, not a third-party aggregator, and the board resolution authorising the injection and share allotment must be pre-filed with the receiving Gibraltar bank. For amounts exceeding EUR 100,000 (or GIP/GBP sterling equivalent), a statement of source of wealth and confirmation of no OFAC/UK Sanctions nexus is required before credit. CHF/EUR/GBP settlement is via the Gibraltar bank's correspondent accounts with BoE and ECB, with a 1-2 business-day T+1 value date. Where the parent is funding via crypto or virtual-asset conversion, the Gibraltar bank will require liquidation via a compliant exchange and a fiat audit trail minimum of 60 days before accepting the fiat proceeds as clean capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlements to EU thermoplastic sheet suppliers (raw PETG and PU aligner film) and dental equipment vendors shall be executed via SWIFT MT103 for amounts under GBP 500,000, using purpose code 'TRADE' with the underlying commercial invoice and Bill of Lading attached to the instruction. Larger raw-material procurement contracts above GBP 500,000 may utilise a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) with 30 to 90-day usance, countersigned by the Gibraltar bank's trade finance desk, payable at sight upon presentation of shipping documents. Urgent UK supplier payments shall clear through the Faster Payments Service (FPS) via the Gibraltar bank's UK settlement membership; EU supplier disbursements use TARGET2 instant payment rails (via SEPA CT) only where the counterparty is an EU-based beneficiary. Commission and royalty out-payments to the Cayman parent are restricted to a quarterly board-approved treasury calendar and must be tagged with purpose code 'ROYL' to maintain transfer-pricing defensibility. Stripe platform payouts of card receivables settle daily in GBP to the operational account before any onward FX conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forward FX contracts (GIP/GBP against USD and EUR) with tenors up to 12 months, executed under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or title-transfer collateral arrangements with Gibraltar International Bank
FX swaps (swap de change) covering T/N to 6-month maturities for interbank liquidity mismatches between Stripe settlement currency and supplier currency
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and GBP/EUR) for conversion of trade receivables into settlement currency with quarterly net settlement

Vanilla FX options (European style, GBPUSD and EURUSD puts/calls) for downside protection on dental aligner export receivables, available from Lombard Odier and Jyske for minimum notional of USD 2 million
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are NOT permissible in this jurisdiction pair as GIP, GBP, EUR, and USD all clear as deliverable currencies without convertibility constraints

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Name of annual return, corporate declaration, or franchise filing
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalties and timeline triggering administrative strike-off
